item.content:encoded:
Grove Account

UEBT will register each (Potential) Certificate Holder (CH) and Certification Body (CB) contact in the Grove platform once UEBT approves the company’s application for certification or upon approval of a new CB auditor.

 

Article Information

Creating your password

 

Each contact will receive an email titled “Welcome to the UEBT Grove Community.”

In this email, click the link “join the UEBT Grove community here” to create your password.

You will then be prompted to select a secure authentication method as an additional security step.

 

You will then have two options:

Option 1: Passkey

 

Click on “Register passkey.”

Then click “Continue.”

 

You will be asked to enter your PIN. This is normally the same PIN you use to log in to your computer.

 

You should then be able to access Grove.

Option 2: Another authentication method

 

If you do not want to, or cannot, use the Passkey security authentication method, you can choose another authentication method.

Select whichever option works best for you, depending on the apps and devices you have available.

Once you have completed the authentication steps, you will be prompted to create a password.

You will then have access to the new Grove main page.

Important notes

Our new Grove platform is hosted on Salesforce. If you have used Salesforce before, your Salesforce security authentication method may already have been defined. In that case, you will need to select the appropriate method. If you do not remember which one you previously set up, you can try the different options described above.

If you experience any issues with logging in or authentication, please contact Grove@uebt.org.

item.title: Audit Report
item.dc:creator: admin
item.content:encoded:
Audit Report

Once UEBT has attached the relevant checklist to the audit planning and approved it, the auditor has access to the checklists, also referred to on the platform as ‘evaluations’. This page explains how to consult, complete, review and submit them. 

 

Please note that our IT team is currently still working on making the checklists easier to access and identify and the report review process more user friendly for both auditors and reviewers. The aim is for the audit report submission and review process to become easier for Certification Bodies than it was on the previous Grove platform, so please bear with us while we are working on improving the new platform. 

 

Article Information

Consulting the checklists

 

Once the audit planning has been approved by UEBT, the checklist are available to the auditor. There are two ways to access the checklist via the Grove Homepage: 

Option 1: By scrolling down and selecting the ‘Evaluations’ field directly in the audit. 

Option 2: By going to Programmes at the top and selecting ‘Evaluations’ there. This will bring you to the audit overview, where you need to select the relevant audit. 

Option 1

 

This will directly bring you to the overview of all the checklists attached to this audit. 

Evaluation 1: Field checklist

Evaluation 2: System checklist

Evaluation 3: RA supplement (if UEBT/RA)

Evaluation 4: Membership supplement

Evaluation 5: Evaluation General (General Audit Information)

Please note that our IT team is working on making the different checklists easier identifiable by including an evaluation name and title. 

Option 2

 

This will directly bring you to the overview of all active evaluations (all checklists for all audits, that still need to be completed). 

In this overview, finding the checklists related to the audit you want to complete is a bit more challenging. 

To find your checklists in the overview, you have to select one of the evaluations (checklists) that is related to your audit. 

Once you are in the checklist, you can click on ‘Related Evaluations’ to find all of the checklists related to your audit. 

Evaluation 1: Field checklist

Evaluation 2: System checklist

Evaluation 3: RA supplement (if UEBT/RA)

Evaluation 4: Membership supplement

Evaluation 5: Evaluation General (General Audit Information)

Completing the audit report

 

Please note that each checklist/evaluation listed above (1-5) needs to be completed separately.

The platform uses an autosave function, meaning that your changes to the checklist will be saved automatically, provided that you have a stable internet connection. 

While you are working on completing the checklists, you can change the status of the audit report to ‘Incomplete’ under the Evaluation General checklist, as a reminder for yourself that you are working on completing it.

You do this by clicking on ‘Incomplete’, and selecting ‘Mark as Current Evaluation Status’ on the left side. 

Submitting audit report for CB review

 

Once a checklist is completed, the auditor can submit it by clicking ‘Submit’ on the top right corner. 

Once you submit a checklist, the fields will turn grey on the auditor's side, and he or she can no longer make changes to the checklist. 

Once all the checklists have been submitted, the status of the audit report will now change to 'Evaluation review'. 

The checklists will only be sent to the CB reviewer once all individual checklists have been successfully submitted. 

You can consult this status under the Audit General checklist.

item.title: Audit Planning
item.dc:creator: admin
item.content:encoded:
Planning and Audit on the Grove Platform

Once the (potential) Certificate Holder has submitted a scope to the Grove platform, the audit can be planned by the auditor or coordinator. 

 

Article Information

Creating a new audit

 

To plan a new audit go to the Grove Home page and scroll down.

Under Evaluation by Certification Body fill in: 

  • Program: Certification

  • Organisation: The organisation for which you conduct the audit.

Click ‘Next’. 

Selecting audit scope

 

You are now presented with the Evaluation by Certification Body overview. 

Here, you select the audit scope(s) by ticking the box for the ingredient(s) in the audit scope. 

Then click ‘Next’. 

Please note that each ingredient has a separate scope form, so please make sure you select all the ingredient scope forms in the scope of the audit. 

If there are no scopes in this overview, this means that the (potential) CH has not uploaded their scope(s) correctly. Please ask the company to do so, before planning your audit in the system. 

Once you have selected the scope, the audit planning will appear. 

Click on ‘View planning record’ on the left. 

 

The audit has now been created.

To verify if the correct scopes are attached to the audit planning, next to the Details button, select ‘Scopes’.  

You will now see an overview of all the scopes. 

To see only the ones that are attached to your current audit, press button ‘Show only scopes attached to this planning’. 

Reviewing audit scope

 

To review if the scope(s) are completed, please click on each scope under the Scope Name header. 

Here, please carefully review whether the following sections are correctly completed for each scope:

Natural Material

 

  • Ingredient: The ingredient name, plant part, and state.

  • Type of production system: Either cultivated or wild-harvested.

  • Ingredient state: Either fresh, dried, or essential oil.

Additional information

 

  • Organisation at Source (OaS): The organisation that cultivates or collects the ingredient.

  • BAP associated?: This box should be ticked if there is an approved BAP by UEBT for this ingredient.

Certification

 

  • Plan to certify/verify this scope? This box should be ticked.

  • Year of audit: The year in which the audit was conducted. 

  • Type of Certification: One of the following options:

    1) UEBT Ingredient (Botanicals) Certification, 

    2) UEBT RA (Herbs and Spices – Identity Preserved) or 

    3) UEBT RA (Herbs and Spices – Segregated) 

  • Regenerative add-on: This box should be ticked if the audit is for a UEBT or UEBT/RA regenerative certification audit.

  • Number of sub-suppliers

  • Number of farms

  • Number of farmers

  • Number of workers

Harvesting 

 

  • Size of sourcing area (Ha)

  • Estimation of yield (tonnes/Ha)

  • Conversion rate – plant to natural raw material: The percentage should be entered as a number. For example, for 50%, enter 50; for 0.005%, enter 0.005.

  • Fresh ingredient to certify (tonnes)

  • Volume of fresh plant this year

  • Volume of fresh plant last year

  • Volume sold as certified (in the previous year)

  • Volume to be included in the certificate

Request scope update

 

Only if changes to the scope are needed, please go to the top and press the ‘Request More Information’ button. 

A field appears in which you can leave comments to request changes to the scope form from the CH. 

If no changes are needed, you can skip this step. 

Please bear in mind that in the months following the launch of the new platform, notifications may not be automatically sent yet. In this case, please send an email to the CH directly to request the changes. 

Audit Details

In the audit Details section, please fill in:

 

Dates

  • Evaluation start date: Audit start date.

  • Evaluation end date: Audit end date.

  • Evaluation start date confirmed: Tick this box if the start date has been confirmed. The CH will then receive an automatic notification that the audit date has been confirmed. 

    Please bear in mind that in the months following the launch of the new platform, notifications may not be automatically sent yet. 

     

Team

  • CB coordinator

  • CB reviewer

  • Lead auditor

     

Only if appliable:

  • Second auditor

  • Third auditor

  • Trainee auditor / Observer

Submit audit planning

 

Once you have reviewed the scope and completed the audit details above, under the audit Details, go to ‘Status’ field and select ‘UEBT Review’. 

You have now submitted your audit planning for review by UEBT.

Please bear in mind that in the months following the launch of the new platform, notifications may not be automatically sent yet. In this case, please send an email to certification@uebt.org directly to notify the UEBT certification team that a new audit planning has been submitted for review. 

Request for changes

 

After you have submitted the audit planning, UEBT reviews it and adds the relevant checklists for your evaluation. 

When changes to the audit planning are needed, you will receive a notification from UEBT on the platform or via email. If the audit planning is returned to you in status:

 

  • Incomplete, this means that not all required fields have been completed. 

  • Rejected, this means that not all information is correctly filled in. 

 

Audit planning approval

 

If all information is correctly filled in, the certification team will approve the planning. 

You can consult the current status of the audit planning on the Homepage of the Grove platform. 

Once approved, you can consult the checklists to be evaluated under ‘Evaluations’ and complete the audit report.  

For guidance on how to complete and submit the audit report, please visit the Audit Report Submission guidance.

item.title: Scope Submission by the CH
item.dc:creator: admin
item.content:encoded:
Scope Submission

Before your Certification Body (CB) can create an audit on the Grove platform, the (potential) Certificate Holder (CH) needs to submit the scope form on the platform first. This guidance explains how to do so. 

 

You have to submit your scope form(s) each year, prior to your annual audit.

 

Article Information

You have to submit a scope form each year for each ingredient, prior to your annual audit. 

To submit a scope form, go to the Grove platform homepage and click “Scopes” at the top.

 

Cloning a scope

On the Scope overview page, you can clone a scope from a previous year and edit it by going to the scope you would like to clone

Now click the arrow on the right and select “Clone”. 

Creating a new scope

If there is no existing scope for this ingredient yet, you can create a new scope on the Scope overview page. If you have cloned an existing scope, please skip this step.  

To create a new scope, select “New Scope” in the top right corner. 

Once you have cloned an existing or opened a new scope, you will now see the scope form you just created. 

On the scope form, please make sure that the following sections are correctly filled in:

Scope details

 

  • Scope name: Any name you wish to give to your scope that makes it easily recognizable, e.g. year/audit date_company name_ingredient.

  • Year of the audit: Year in which the audit is conducted.

  • Client reference: No need to complete this field.

 

Natural Material

 

  • Ingredient: Select the ingredient, including the ingredient name, plant part, and state.

    If you cannot find the ingredient, select “Create new ingredient” and enter the plant species, part, and state of the ingredient. 

    Then click “Save Ingredient.”

  • Type of production system: Select either cultivated or wild-harvested.

  • Ingredient state: Select fresh, dried, or essential oil.

Location

 

  • Country oOrganisation at Source (OaS): The organisation that cultivates or collects the ingredient.

  • BAP associated?: Tick this box if there is an approved BAP by UEBT for the ingredient.d area?: Tick this box where applicable.

 

Additional information

 

  • Organisation at Source (OaS): The organisation that cultivates or collects the ingredient.

  • BAP associated?: Tick this box if there is an approved BAP by UEBT for the ingredient.

Certification

 

Under Type of certification, select the option that corresponds to the certification being planned

  1. UEBT Ingredient (Botanicals) Certification – for UEBT-only (and regenerative) certification.

  2. UEBT RA (Herbs and Spices – Identity Preserved) – for UEBT/RA certification where the OaS directly responsible for the cultivation or wild collection of the ingredient is the Certificate Holder (CH).

  3. UEBT RA (Herbs and Spices – Segregated) – for UEBT/RA certification where the company not directly responsible for the cultivation or wild collection of the ingredient is the CH, and sources the ingredient from a farm, farmer cooperative, or another local organisation (OaS).

     

  • Regenerative add-on: Tick this box if the audit is for a UEBT or UEBT/RA regenerative certification audit.

  • Number of sub-suppliers

  • Number of farmers

  • Number of farms

  • Number of workers

Harvesting data

 

Complete the following fields:

  1. UEBT Ingredient (Botanicals) Certification – for UEBT-only (and regenerative) certification.

  2. UEBT RA (Herbs and Spices – Identity Preserved) – for UEBT/RA certification where the OaS directly responsible for the cultivation or wild collection of the ingredient is the Certificate Holder (CH).

  3. UEBT RA (Herbs and Spices – Segregated) – for UEBT/RA certification where the company not directly responsible for the cultivation or wild collection of the ingredient is the CH, and sources the ingredient from a farm, farmer cooperative, or another local organisation (OaS).

     

  • Size of sourcing area (Ha)

  • Conversion rate – plant to natural raw material: Enter the percentage as a number. For example, for 50%, enter 50; for 0.005%, enter 0.005.

  • Volume of fresh plant this year

  • Volume sold as certified (in the previous year)

  • Estimation of yield: In tonnes/ha

  • Fresh ingredient to certify: In tonnes

  • Volume of fresh plant last year: In tonnes

  • Volume to be included in the certificate: In tonnes

 

Tick “Put this scope forward for Certification/Verification with UEBT.”

Then click “Create Scope” at the bottom of the page.

Editing an existing scope

 

Once the scope has been created, you will automatically be taken to the Scopes overview page. 

You can click on the scope name to open and edit the scope. Alternatively, click the arrow on the right-hand side to edit, clone, or delete the scope:

Open the scope you have just created and scroll down. You should now see the following sections

  • Harvest/Collection Period

  • Agrochemical Application Period

  • Scope Documents

Harvest/Collection Periods

Click “Add Period” on the right-hand side and enter the start and end dates of the harvest or collection period.
If the ingredient has multiple harvest or collection periods, add each period separately.

Agrochemical Application Period

Click “Add Period” and enter the start and end dates of the agrochemical application period.
These dates can be estimates if you do not know the exact dates.
If no agrochemicals are applied, you can leave this section blank.

Scope Documents

This is where you upload the certification scope form.

Submitting this form is still a mandatory step for audit planning.

 

 Under Category, select the type of document that you uploaded:

  • For the Certification Scope form, select Supply Chain Structure.

  • If you have an approved BAP by UEBT, upload it and select BAP as the category.

 

The Description field does not need to be completed.

 

Once you have completed these sections, click ‘Save’ at the top right corner. You have now successfully entered your scope in the system. 

Please fill in a separate scope form for each ingredient in your certification scope. 

 

Note that you do not need to upload the Supply Chain Structure Excel to each individual ingredient scope form. 

If the Supply Chain Structure is attached to one ingredient scope form, this is sufficient. 

Please do fill in the Category field for each ingredient scope form, also when no document was uploaded.

Editing your Scope

 

Once you have added your audit scope(s) to the Grove platform, the CB may now select the scope(s) to plan your audit. 

When the CB reviews your scope and concludes that one of the fields is not (correctly) filled in, they may send you a request to edit your scope form. 

When this happens, you can always revisit your scope by going to the Grove Home page and selecting “Scopes” at the top. 

You can then select the scope you want to edit, click on the arrow at the right, and select “Edit”, to make the changes requested by the CB.

Once you have made the changes, please scroll up and select ‘Save changes’. 

Please notify the CB by email.

item.title: MFA Setup
item.dc:creator: admin
item.content:encoded:
MFA Setup

Overview

Multi-factor authentication (MFA) adds an extra verification step to help protect your Grove account. Before using Grove, all users should complete MFA setup and verify that their chosen authentication method works correctly.

 

This article explains prerequisites, available verification options, setup steps, common issues, and where to get additional help.

Step-by-Step MFA Setup

 

Step 1: Sign in

Sign in using your Grove account credentials. If MFA has not yet been configured, you will be prompted to begin the registration process.

Step 2: Choose a verification method

Select the verification option that has been approved for your account.

 

Step 3: Configure your authenticator

 

  • Open your authenticator application.
  • Add a new work account.
  • Scan the QR code presented during setup when applicable.

  • Complete any registration prompts shown by the authenticator application.

     

Step 4: Verify the connection

Enter the verification code or approve the authentication request when prompted. Successful verification confirms that the method is linked to your account.

 

Step 5: Complete registration

 

Finish the setup workflow and return to the sign-in experience. Test the selected verification method to confirm it works correctly.

 

Common Issues

I am not receiving prompts or codes

  • Confirm the correct account is registered.
  • Check device connectivity.
  • Retry the verification process.

The verification code is rejected

  • Generate a new code.
  • Ensure the code is entered before it expires.
  • Verify the correct account is selected in the authenticator application.

Recovery and Troubleshooting

Changed or lost device

  • Contact support if you can no longer access your registered verification method.
  • Do not create duplicate accounts.

Registration does not complete

  • Sign out and start the process again.
  • Try a supported browser.
  • Contact support if the issue persists.

item.title: Audit Process
item.dc:creator: admin
item.content:encoded:
Audit Process

Overview

This guidance article explains the Grove audit process for Members and Certification Bodies. The audit process helps ensure that required information, evidence, reviews, and decisions are completed in a structured and transparent sequence.

Users should understand what preparation is required, what evidence may be requested, how audits progress through each stage, and where to obtain support when questions arise.

Stage 1: Preparation and Readiness

Before audit activities begin, organisations should ensure that required information is available and up to date.

Typical preparation activities

  • Confirm certification scope information.
  • Review required documentation.

  • Don't forget the cheese.

  • Identify key contacts and participants.
  • Prepare supporting evidence and records.
  • Address known information gaps before audit planning.

Good preparation reduces delays during later audit stages.

Evidence Expectations

Evidence supports the audit process and helps reviewers assess submitted information.

  • Policies and procedures.
  • Operational records.
  • Training records.
  • Monitoring information.
  • Supporting documentation requested during the audit process.

Evidence should be complete, current, and available when requested.

Stage 2: Audit Planning

Audit planning begins when prerequisite application and scope activities have been completed. Planning activities may include assigning a Certification Body, identifying auditors, confirming readiness, and preparing the audit schedule.

Planning objectives

  • Confirm audit requirements.
  • Assign appropriate resources.
  • Communicate expectations and timelines.
  • Establish audit readiness.
  • Prepare records required for audit execution.

During this stage, Members and Certification Bodies should ensure that communication channels remain active and that requested information is provided promptly.

Stage 3: Audit Execution

Once planning is complete, audit activities can begin. Auditors review information, assess evidence, and complete required audit activities.

  • Review submitted information.
  • Assess supporting evidence.
  • Record findings and observations.
  • Request clarification where necessary.
  • Update audit status as activities progress.

Stage 4: Evaluation and Review

Following audit execution, submitted materials are reviewed to determine whether additional information is required and whether the process can move forward.

  • Review audit outputs.
  • Validate evidence completeness.
  • Assess findings and observations.
  • Record review outcomes.
  • Communicate follow-up requirements.

Audience Notes for Members

  • Maintain accurate and current records.
  • Respond to information requests promptly.
  • Provide evidence in the requested format.
  • Track actions arising from audit findings.
  • Monitor communications and status updates.

Audience Notes for Certification Bodies

  • Coordinate planning activities.
  • Manage auditor assignments where applicable.
  • Review evidence and findings consistently.
  • Record outcomes and status changes accurately.
  • Support communication throughout the audit lifecycle.

Stage 5: Decision and Outcomes

After review activities are complete, the process moves toward an outcome or decision stage.

Users should monitor communications and complete any requested follow-up activities within required timelines.

Corrective Actions and Follow-Up

Where findings require attention, corrective actions may be created and tracked until completion.

  • Review assigned actions.
  • Provide supporting evidence.
  • Track completion progress.
  • Respond to review feedback.
  • Confirm closure when requirements are met.

Related Guidance

  • Certification Planning
  • FAQs
  • Contact Support

item.title: Audit planning for Certification Bodies
item.dc:creator: admin
item.content:encoded:
Audit planning for Certification Bodies

Before planning starts

Audit planning begins once the applicant or certificate holder has contacted an authorised Certification Body. The CB should then contact UEBT to confirm the organisation profile, certification scope and any audit instructions that apply to the case.

  • Use the UEBT audit plan template, or an approved equivalent.
  • Base the plan on the confirmed scope, UEBT instructions, client information, previous audit history, risk information and applicable law assessments.
  • Assign an audit team with the required competence for the scope, locations, supply chains and languages involved.

1. Confirm scope

Check the certification scope, sites, processes, supply chains and products to be audited. Identify any exclusions, sampling needs and scope changes since the previous audit.

2. Build the plan

Set the audit objectives, type, dates, locations, programme, timing and duration. Include audit team roles, expected organisation participants and resources required.

3. Share and prepare

Upload the final plan to Grove and share it with the auditee on time. Complete preparation activities before the audit starts.

Planning milestones

Planning inputs

  • Certification Scope Form
  • UEBT audit instructions
  • Country risk assessment
  • Applicable laws assessment
  • Previous work plans and audit history
  • Biodiversity Action Plan, where applicable
  • Monitoring system documentation, including IMS or LMS
  • Client risk assessments and supporting compliance documentation

Audit plan content

  • Audit objectives and audit type
  • Applicable standards, checklists and reference documents
  • Scope, sites and processes to be audited
  • Dates, locations, programme, timing and duration
  • Audit team roles and responsibilities
  • Expected organisation participants
  • Resource allocation and sampling approach, where relevant

High-risk supply chains

Where a certification audit involves a high-risk supply chain, plan earlier and ask UEBT for specific instructions. Additional requirements may include expanded sampling, interviews, experts or public consultation.

  • Notify UEBT 12 weeks before the audit where additional instructions may be needed.
  • UEBT may provide additional scope instructions 10 weeks before the audit.
  • Share the draft audit plan 8 weeks before the audit date.

Readiness check for CBs

  • The audit scope is current and matches the client’s certification request.
  • UEBT instructions and risk information have been incorporated.
  • The audit team has the right competence and role allocation.
  • Sites, participants, languages, logistics and timings are confirmed.
  • Sampling is justified and documented where relevant.
  • The plan has been uploaded to Grove and shared with the auditee within the required timeframe.

item.title: Article structure
item.dc:creator: admin
item.content:encoded:
Article Structure

Purpose of this standard

This page defines the standard structure for Grove guidance and help articles. Certification team editors should use this model to create consistent, easy-to-maintain content for Members and Certification Bodies.

A consistent structure helps users quickly find the information they need, improves content quality, simplifies review activities, and supports long-term maintenance of Grove guidance.

Core principles

  • Start with the information users need most.
  • Use clear section headings.
  • Separate audience-specific guidance where necessary.
  • Include troubleshooting and support paths.
  • Assign ownership and review responsibilities.
  • Keep related resources visible and current.

Required article sections

SectionPurpose
OverviewExplain what the article covers and why it matters.
AudienceIdentify who should use the guidance.
PrerequisitesList information, access, or preparation required.
Procedure or GuidanceMain instructions, process, or explanation.
TroubleshootingCommon issues and resolution guidance.
Related ResourcesLinks to supporting pages and resources.
Review OwnershipDefine content owner and review cycle.

Recommended article metadata

  • Article title
  • Audience
  • Category
  • Summary
  • Content owner
  • Publication status
  • Last reviewed date
Every published article should have a clearly identified owner who is responsible for accuracy and periodic review.

Standard article template

1. Overview

Provide a short introduction explaining the purpose of the guidance, the business context, and the outcome the reader should expect.

2. Audience

  • Members
  • Certification Bodies
  • Both audiences

3. Prerequisites

  • Required access
  • Required information
  • Required preparation activities

4. Steps or Guidance

Present the main content in a logical sequence. Use numbered steps for procedures and descriptive headings for reference guidance.

5. Troubleshooting

IssuePossible CauseResolution
[Add issue][Add cause][Add resolution]

6. Related Resources

Link users to supporting guidance, FAQs, resources, or support channels.

7. Review Ownership

Document the owner, review frequency, and escalation path for content updates.

Content quality checklist

  • Title clearly reflects the content.
  • Audience is identified.
  • Instructions are complete and accurate.
  • Terminology is consistent.
  • Links are current.
  • Troubleshooting information is included when applicable.
  • Ownership information is present.
  • Review date is current.

Related Grove Resources

  • First Login
  • MFA Setup
  • Certification Planning
  • Audit Process
  • Contact Support

Ownership and review model

Every article should have a named content owner responsible for maintaining accuracy, coordinating updates, and responding to feedback.

RoleResponsibility
Content OwnerMaintains article accuracy and completeness.
ReviewerValidates guidance before publication.
EditorEnsures structure, formatting, and consistency.

Review guidance content regularly and update ownership whenever responsibilities change.
item.excerpt:encoded: Define a repeatable structure for Grove help pages. Give editors a consistent model for overview, audience, prerequisites, steps, troubleshooting, related links, and review ownership.

item.dc:creator: admin
item.content:encoded:
FAQs

First Login GuidanceFind help for first-time access, sign-in expectations, and common login questions.
MFA SetupReview authentication setup guidance and answers to common MFA questions.
Certification PlanningUnderstand planning activities, responsibilities, and preparation requirements.
Audit ProcessExplore audit stages, evidence expectations, and process-related FAQs.
Contact SupportGet help when you cannot find an answer or need additional assistance.

About this FAQ page

This page provides quick answers to common Grove questions for Members and Certification Bodies. Questions are grouped by topic so you can quickly find the guidance most relevant to your activity. For detailed instructions, use the related guidance articles available throughout the site.

Audience

  • Members
  • Certification Bodies
  • Users requiring account access assistance

Topics covered

  • First Login
  • Multi-Factor Authentication (MFA)
  • Certification Planning
  • Audit Process
  • Support and Assistance

First Login FAQs

QuestionAnswer
How do I sign in for the first time?Use your Grove access link and follow the sign-in prompts. If access fails, contact support with your account details.
What do I need before signing in?Ensure you have received your access invitation and have access to the authentication method required for your account.
What should I do if I cannot access my account?Review the First Login guidance page and contact support if the issue continues.

Member Tip

Confirm that your account information is current before attempting first access.

MFA Setup FAQs

QuestionAnswer
What MFA method should I use?Use the approved authentication method listed in your onboarding instructions. If your method is unavailable, contact support.
When should MFA be configured?Complete MFA setup before beginning regular use of Grove.
What if I cannot complete verification?Review the MFA Setup guidance and contact support for assistance.

Good Practice

Keep your authentication method available whenever you need to access Grove.

Certification Planning FAQs

For Members

QuestionAnswer
What should Members prepare before planning?Members should confirm scope, key dates, required inputs, and internal contacts before starting planning.
Why is planning important?Effective planning helps ensure activities, responsibilities, and required information are ready when needed.
Where can I find planning guidance?Use the Certification Planning page for detailed information.

Audit Process FAQs

For Certification Bodies

QuestionAnswer
What should Certification Bodies expect during audit review?Certification Bodies should review evidence, record findings, and follow the agreed audit sequence in Grove.
What information should be prepared?Ensure required evidence and supporting information are available according to process requirements.
Where can I learn more about audit stages?Refer to the Audit Process guidance page.

Support FAQs

QuestionAnswer
Who should I contact for general help?Use the Contact Support page to choose the support route for your issue type.
Can I get help with login or MFA issues?Yes. Select the support route that matches your issue category.
When should I contact support?Contact support when guidance does not resolve your issue or additional assistance is required.
Use guidance articles first, then contact support if you need further help.

Related Guidance

  • First Login
  • MFA Setup
  • Certification Planning
  • Audit Process

Before raising a request, review the relevant guidance article and FAQs where available. When contacting support, include clear details about the issue, affected process, and any relevant screenshots or error messages.

  • Preparation for audit activities

If you are unable to access Grove because of login or MFA issues, select the appropriate support route as soon as possible. Include the following information:

  • The date and time the issue occurred
  • Any error message shown
  • Screenshots where appropriate

Providing complete information helps support teams understand and investigate the issue more efficiently.

  • MFA Setup

  • Audit Process
  • FAQs

item.title: Certification Planning
item.dc:creator: admin
item.content:encoded:
Certification Planning

Audit ProcessUnderstand the activities that follow certification planning and audit preparation.
Guidance ResourcesAccess supporting guidance materials and reference documents related to certification activities.
Contact SupportGet help if you need clarification on planning responsibilities or requirements.

Purpose of Certification Planning

Certification planning is the stage where Members, Certification Bodies, and supporting teams prepare for a certification audit. Effective planning helps ensure that the correct scope, participants, documentation, timelines, and review activities are established before audit activities begin.

This guidance provides a structured overview of responsibilities, required inputs, key milestones, and preparation expectations for all parties involved.

Good planning reduces delays, supports audit readiness, and helps ensure that certification activities proceed efficiently.

Audience

AudienceHow to use this guidance
MembersPrepare certification scope information, review planning requests, provide required inputs, and respond to clarification requests.
Certification BodiesCoordinate audit planning, review submitted scope information, assign audit resources, and prepare the audit schedule.

Planning Milestones

  1. Application or eligibility approval
  2. Planning initiation
  3. Scope information collection and review
  4. Audit team assignment
  5. Audit scheduling
  6. Planning review and completion
  7. Transition to audit execution

Each milestone should be completed before progressing to the next stage.

Required Inputs

  • Organisation details
  • Contact information
  • Certification scope information
  • Location information
  • Ingredient or material information where applicable
  • Audit availability and scheduling preferences
  • Supporting planning documentation

Incomplete information may result in additional review cycles or planning delays.

Roles and Responsibilities

RoleKey Responsibilities
MemberProvide and maintain accurate certification scope information, review requests, submit required documentation, and respond to planning questions.
Certification BodyCoordinate planning activities, review scope information, assign audit personnel, establish audit dates, and prepare audit arrangements.
Certification TeamReview planning information where required, provide guidance, and support oversight activities.
AuditorParticipate once assigned, review planning information, and prepare for audit execution.

Responsibility Principle

Members are responsible for the accuracy of submitted information. Certification Bodies are responsible for coordinating and managing planning activities. All parties should communicate changes promptly to maintain planning accuracy.

Guidance for Members

  • Review all organisation and contact information before submission.
  • Confirm certification scope information is complete and current.
  • Respond promptly to requests for clarification.
  • Monitor notifications and planning updates.
  • Prepare supporting documents before audit scheduling is finalized.

Where previous certification information exists, review it carefully and update any changes relevant to the upcoming certification cycle.

Guidance for Certification Bodies

  • Review submitted planning information for completeness.
  • Confirm audit scope and planning assumptions.
  • Assign appropriate audit personnel.
  • Coordinate scheduling with the Member.
  • Identify information gaps early.
  • Complete planning review before audit execution begins.

Clear communication during planning helps reduce audit delays and improves readiness for all participants.

Preparation Checklist

  • Organisation details reviewed
  • Contacts confirmed
  • Scope information validated
  • Supporting documents prepared
  • Audit availability confirmed
  • Questions resolved
  • Planning status reviewed

Common Causes of Delay

  • Incomplete scope information
  • Missing documentation
  • Unclear ownership of actions
  • Late responses to requests
  • Scheduling conflicts
  • Unresolved planning questions

Addressing these issues early helps keep certification activities on schedule.

Related Guidance

  • First Login
  • MFA Setup
  • Audit Process
  • FAQs

Key Takeaways

Certification planning establishes the foundation for a successful audit. Members should focus on providing accurate and complete information, while Certification Bodies should coordinate planning activities, scheduling, and review processes. Early preparation and timely communication help reduce delays and improve audit readiness.
